messages.subject: httr:POST in Shiny Server Application
parts:
Forgive me if this is an obvious answer, but I am attempting to run the following code in a Shiny application.  It works great when I run it locally, but when I deploy it to Shiny Server, I get an error back.  Could someone point me towards the differences between this code running on Windows versus Linux?  Thanks!

r <- POST("http://serverinfo", 
body = list(program='programname',
 textvar1="directfromR",
 filestamp=1234))
stop_for_status(r)
content(r, "parsed", "text/html")

messages.subject: Re: httr:POST in Shiny Server Application
parts:
Sorry Andy,
I mistakenly sent an email as opposed to responding on the forum.

Here's what I sent followed by the answer to your question.

I'm thinking it's not a Shiny issue necessarily, because I have the same issue with the raw code.  This is what I get back with verbose():

 HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
<- Cache-Control: no-cache
<- Pragma: no-cache
<- Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
<- Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
<- Connection: Keep-Alive
<- Content-Length: 1126

I also noticed that when I run it from windows, it pulls the server name off of the address, but in Linux, the whole thing is there:

windows:
POST /folder/guest HTTP/1.1
-> User-Agent: curl/7.19.6 Rcurl/1.95.4.1 httr/0.5
-> Host: servername:90

linux:
POST servername:90/folder/guest HTTP/1.1
-> User-Agent: curl/7.19.7 Rcurl/1.95.4.3 httr/0.5
-> Host: servername:90

Again, doesn't seem like a Shiny issue, but I'm happy to hear any suggestions you may have.

You asked: It seems strange to me that the HTTP request would be malformed depending on which platform you are using. Are you sure the URL you are using is well formed?

The expected result comes back from my windows machine, so I'm assuming it is well formed.  Is there some other way to know?
